title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly pilot sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed VPC peering and routing issues, kernel/runtime upgrade plan, performance tuning (KV cache, batching), and outstanding security docs. Agreed on next steps for benchmarks and a short validation window for runtime 2.1 rollout.
topics: KV prefix cache tuning and batching
Security artifacts: SOC2, audit logs, KMS/SAML
next_steps: Redwood to share runtime 2.1 release notes and kernel logs (Samira)
Customer to run bench harness with pinned dataset and share results (Marta)
Ben to confirm KMS key rotation schedule and share access matrix (Ben)
Schedule in-person troubleshooting session if peering not stable by 2026-09-28 (Jordan)
action_items: Samira Khan (Redwood) - provide kernel selection logs and a short explanation of 2.1 perf delta by 2026-09-24
Marta Silva (ClearWave) - run 10k-token benchmark with KV cache enabled and share CSV by 2026-09-25
Ben Torres (ClearWave) - confirm KMS cross-account access and supply key ARN by 2026-09-26

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Alan Moore (ClearWave CTO), Priya Ramesh (Infra), Ben Torres (Security), Marta Silva (ML)

Summary: weekly check-in for Redwood Private VPC pilot; main threads: networking flaky routes, runtime upgrade, perf tuning.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll start in a minute. uh — quick roll call?
[00:12] Alan Moore: Alan here.
[00:14] Priya Ramesh: Priya.
[00:16] Ben Torres: Ben.
[00:18] Marta Silva: Marta.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: great. Jordan from Redwood, Samira and Liam are on. Agenda: peering status, routing/NAT, runtime 2.1 upgrade, perf numbers, security docs, and next steps.
[00:38] Samira Khan: quick recap — last week we saw intermittent packet loss on the peered subnet, route table mismatch; Redwood config showed a missing propagate route for the bastion subnets, which we patched but it looks like there's still some residual caching on your side, maybe 5-10 minute TTLs.
[00:58] Priya Ramesh: yeah we saw inconsistent route propagation. sometimes traffic to the serving pods goes out via the internet gateway then back in, which spikes latency. we are checking route table prop and VPN tunnel state.
[01:20] Ben Torres: to add, from security we saw a couple of rejected flows where source IP was rewritten — looks like the NAT gateway config combined with our Egress policy is messing up the health-check IPs.
[01:36] Samira Khan: right, that explains some of the 200-300ms spikes in the perf runs. If the health checks hit the wrong IP the runtime will reinitialize the KV cache, so you'll see cold-cache hiccups.
[01:54] Marta Silva: that might be why our 1M-token run last night had a couple of long tails. we lost 4 traces where latency jumped.
[02:06] Jordan Lee: OK, action: Priya to confirm route table propagation TTL and update us when fixed. Ben to confirm NAT config. We'll re-run a short smoke after those two items.

[02:22] Priya Ramesh: noted. on another note, what's the status of the runtime upgrade? Samira you were testing kernel selection changes in 2.1?
[02:34] Samira Khan: yes, on the Redwood side 2.1 includes a new kernel selector that biases for attention layout for the open models we tested. in our lab runs we saw 8-12% token-per-second improvement on A100 and about 4-6% on older Ampere variants. but there are a couple of edge cases — very short context workloads can regress slightly.
[02:58] Alan Moore: are there compatibility concerns for our model artifacts? we have a pinned LM fork and custom tokenizer.
[03:08] Samira Khan: should be compatible — we tested with your artifact from last week, but we wanted to run your full benchmark to be sure. also worth noting we changed some default kv cache eviction heuristics, so cache sizing might need adjustment.
[03:26] Marta Silva: can you clarify the kv cache change? last time you said KV cache eviction was more aggressive. that could impact embeddings or long chat sessions.
[03:36] Samira Khan: correct, eviction is slightly more aggressive to reduce memory pressure for multi-tenant hosts; however in private VPC we can tune that knob to be less aggressive since you reserve capacity. we'll provide config flags: kv.cache.eviction.threshold and kv.cache.prefetch.window.
[03:58] Priya Ramesh: perfect. we also ran into an issue with the sidecar proxy health-check path rewriting traffic to 127.0.0.1 which caused the service to appear unhealthy to the load balancer. that was a config diff from our config repo vs the template.
[04:18] Samira Khan: yeah we've seen that when people override the proxy section. best practice is to keep the lb health path aligned with our health-port. we'll document that.

[04:30] Jordan Lee: moving to routing — Samira, quick note about fallback: we can configure automatic fallback to Redwood hosted endpoints if the private cluster reports >10% error rate for 3 minutes. would you want that enabled for the pilot?
[04:48] Ben Torres: from security perspective fallback to hosted is a no-go unless we have encryption in transit end-to-end and contractual assurance. we need SSO audit logs to show data paths.
[05:02] Liam Ortiz: totally hear that. fallback is optional and can be scoped — we can restrict to metadata-only flows for the pilot, or anonymize payloads. We'll draft options.
[05:18] Alan Moore: prefer no fallback for now, unless we can guarantee payload sanitization.

[05:28] Marta Silva: on perf monitoring, we pulled the sample logs and noticed KV cache hit-rate was 68% on average. we expected >80% for our workload. any tuning suggestions?
[05:40] Samira Khan: couple of knobs — increase prefix caching window, adjust batching target and prefetch. also kernel selection in 2.1 reduces per-token compute so cooler host means better hit rates indirectly.
[05:56] Marta Silva: can you send recommended config with sample values?
[05:58] Samira Khan: yes, will send sample config.

[06:04] Priya Ramesh: another infra note — the NFS mount for model artifacts experienced a few timeouts during parallel pulls. we might switch to a pre-warm step or use an artifact cache.
[06:16] Samira Khan: we recommend artifact prefetch per node, or using our S3 proxy which does LRU caching. we'll include a script.

[06:28] Jordan Lee: Security checklist — Ben, you had questions on KMS cross-account and key rotation?
[06:36] Ben Torres: yea, main ask: we need to know whether Redwood will ever hold plaintext model weights or if everything stays encrypted with our KMS. also rotation windows and audit logs.
[06:46] Samira Khan: in Private mode, keys remain in your KMS; Redwood never holds plaintext. we store only ciphertext and the runtime decrypts in-memory. rotation is handled by you; we can support automatic key updates but need the ARN/share time to coordinate. audit logs: we have hooks to forward SG audit events to your SIEM.
[07:04] Ben Torres: can you show the audit hook config?
[07:07] Jordan Lee: we'll share the security pack with the hook samples.

[07:16] Marta Silva: back to performance — we ran a test comparing quantized 4-bit model vs FP16 and saw a small quality drop on our rerank tasks. any guidance?
[07:28] Samira Khan: recommended approach: try q4_0 for inference with validation set. if quality drops for rerank, keep FP16 for the small rerank model and quantize the large generator. we can recommend hybrid routing at the inference layer.
[07:44] Marta Silva: ok we'll try that split.

[07:50] Priya Ramesh: small nit — the current Helm template uses an older CNI config that doesn't set healthgate annotation and causes a 1s reconciliation delay on pods; can we update the template?
[08:02] Samira Khan: yes we've pushed a patch to the template repo earlier today; Jordan will link it.

[08:10] Jordan Lee: rapid recap: Priya and Ben handle net/NAT and KMS items; Samira send kernel logs, config flags and template link; Marta runs the benchmark and reports back; Jordan sends security pack. sound right?
[08:22] Alan Moore: yes. timeline?
[08:24] Jordan Lee: aiming for all items in the next week; we'll reconvene same time next week to validate. if peering issues persist, we'll do an ad-hoc troubleshooting.

[08:34] Priya Ramesh: quick question — if we do the runtime 2.1 upgrade, what's rollback story?
[08:38] Samira Khan: we have an automatic canary with traffic split; rollback is immediate via the control plane and we keep the previous kernel caches until all sessions drain — usually under 2 minutes for in-flight sessions.
[08:52] Ben Torres: will you provide a short runbook for rollback?
[08:55] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll attach the runbook to the ticket.

[09:02] Marta Silva: one more item — can Redwood provide a sample script to drive longer chat sessions for quality eval? we want to reproduce quality regressions vs quantized builds.
[09:12] Samira Khan: yes, we'll share an eval harness and a small sample dataset.

[09:20] Jordan Lee: any blockers from the customer side?
[09:22] Priya Ramesh: just finishing the route table fixes; after that the environment should be stable for more consistent bench runs.
[09:28] Alan Moore: we're good.

[09:30] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. recap and next steps in email. meeting adjourned.

Auto-generated action items (as read out): Priya to confirm route propagation and NAT fix; Ben to share KMS details; Samira to send kernel logs and config flags; Marta to run benchmark; Jordan to send security pack & runbook.

References: Security pack link (shared via email), runtime-2.1-notes.pdf (to be attached), bench-harness repo: github.com/redwood/bench-harness (sample), template patch PR: github.com/redwood/infra-templates/pull/452
